comparison: Perfect agreement on C35-C38 (behavioral characterization of Arc mutants). Both evaluations find the data convincing and well-supported with appropriate statistical testing.
Perfect agreement on C42-C43 (M2 functional role). Both evaluations accept the chemogenetic manipulation data as convincing without concerns.
Perfect agreement on C49-C51 (anatomical tracing data). Both evaluations find the anatomical measurements and normalization approaches appropriate and convincing.

Substantial agreement on calcium imaging data (C52-C56 in OpenEval; C52, C53, C56-C58, C60 in peer review). Both find the imaging data convincing, though peer review groups additional related claims together.

Overlapping evaluation of calcium imaging findings (C57-C60). OpenEval focuses on behavioral replication in imaging animals, while peer review groups these with broader imaging claims. Both find data convincing.
Perfect agreement on C67-C69 (DREADD activation effects). Both evaluations accept the acute DREADD manipulation data and controls as convincing.

Strong agreement on C70-C72 (anatomical restoration). OpenEval notes pooling of injection procedures as potential variability source, while peer review accepts findings without this concern. Both find data convincing overall.
Agreement on C74-C75 (functional restoration). OpenEval evaluates these separately while peer review groups with anatomical data (C70-C72). Both find the functional imaging data convincing.
Strong agreement on rescue findings (C76-C81 in OpenEval; C76, C77, C79, C81 in peer review). Both evaluations find the combined calcium imaging and behavioral rescue data well-supported.

Agreement on C84-C85 (dose-response effects). OpenEval notes lack of clarity on sample size for negative result, while peer review explicitly praises the inverted U-shape dose-response as a strength.
Agreement on C86-C88 (age-dependent effects). OpenEval evaluates separately while peer review groups with other timing/dose experiments. Both find the adolescent-specific effects convincing.
Perfect agreement on C89-C90, C92 (differential effects on amphetamine reactivity). Both evaluations accept the finding that VTA-wide stimulation differs from projection-specific stimulation.
Agreement on C93-C94 (optogenetic validation). OpenEval evaluates these separately while peer review groups with broader projection-specific experiments. Both find the validation data convincing.
